✅ **Prompt Updated**: Showcase Cinematography Sheet (showcase_layout_sheet)

Updated prompt: showcase_layout_sheet

📜 **Version 2** saved (use `action:"history"` to view)

**Changes**: +1 additions, -1 deletions

```diff
===================================================================
--- a/development/showcase_layout_sheet/user-message.md
+++ b/development/showcase_layout_sheet/user-message.md
@@ -3,6 +3,6 @@
 Notes and cards:
 {{context | default("Read the shot row in v3/shots.json (camera, move, led_by, emitter, hue, cards) and the board's §8 camera cards.")}}
 
-Read `v3/creative-spec.md` (D64 moves along leading lines, D74 hue pair per shot, D77 cinematography sheet, D72 craft baseline), `v3/rubric.md` (C5, C6, C24, C25) and the shot row in `v3/shots.json`. Every actor in the shot with keys needs an approved `assets/<actor>/model.json`; a missing one is BLOCKED (run showcase_model_sheet). Choose two to four Composition cards for this shot through the `/inspiration` skill (`eagle_board.py find`, filed with folder, why and source; new cards go on board §8 with eagle:// provenance). Generate ONE cinematography sheet through the `imagegen` tool (`tool:imagegen`), never by hand: `references` are the absolute paths of the actors' model sheets, the chosen camera cards, the shot's object cards and one hue card; the `prompt` names which reference supplies which property and asks for four numbered panels on a pure black field, flat shapes, pale contour, stipple only: PANEL 1 the frame at the START of the shot's camera move (the camera row of the shot, the figure at its on-screen height in percent of frame height), PANEL 2 the frame at the END of the move, PANEL 3 a top-down STAGING PLAN in thin pale lines (actors and objects as marks, the camera as a wedge with the move's arrow, the leading line the move follows drawn through the objects that lead it, suns at the emitter positions), PANEL 4 a SCALE STRIP (the lead actor at panel-1 and panel-2 size on one baseline beside a head-unit ruler, plus the radiance and accent swatches of the D74 pair). `out` is `out/<shot>-layout-<NN>.png`. Measure on the sheet: the lead actor's height in panels 1 and 2 as percent of panel height and in heads (against model.json), the emitter position in each panel as a fraction of panel width and height, the panel-3 camera arrow direction against the shot's move type; reject and regenerate once if the figure's panel-1 height is off the camera row's size by more than 10 points or the hue is not the D74 pair. Write `v3/layouts/<shot>.json` (camera start and end in words, move and led_by, hue, emitter start and end positions, figure heights, heads, panels, cards, sheet sha256, receipt, provisional: true), copy the sheet to `assets/layouts/<shot>-layout-<NN>.png` and `public/assets/layouts/`, lay it into the `LayoutSheet` composition and render one still. The key sheet of this shot is drawn at this camera; the render study measures against this file (C25). The owner approves the sheet from the still.
+Read `v3/creative-spec.md` (D64 moves along leading lines, D74 hue pair per shot, D77 cinematography sheet, D72 craft baseline), `v3/rubric.md` (C5, C6, C24, C25) and the shot row in `v3/shots.json`. Read `v3/timeline.json` for the beats this shot spans (its frames, world and crossing windows) and `v3/blocking/<beat>.json` for the staging already decided per beat: the sheet's panels 1 and 2 draw that staging at the camera, and a staging change the sheet proposes is written back to the blocking file as a diff, not left in the image. Every actor in the shot with keys needs an approved `assets/<actor>/model.json`; a missing one is BLOCKED (run showcase_model_sheet). Choose two to four Composition cards for this shot through the `/inspiration` skill (`eagle_board.py find`, filed with folder, why and source; new cards go on board §8 with eagle:// provenance). Generate ONE cinematography sheet through the `imagegen` tool (`tool:imagegen`), never by hand: `references` are the absolute paths of the actors' model sheets, the chosen camera cards, the shot's object cards and one hue card; the `prompt` names which reference supplies which property and asks for four numbered panels on a pure black field, flat shapes, pale contour, stipple only: PANEL 1 the frame at the START of the shot's camera move (the camera row of the shot, the figure at its on-screen height in percent of frame height), PANEL 2 the frame at the END of the move, PANEL 3 a top-down STAGING PLAN in thin pale lines (actors and objects as marks, the camera as a wedge with the move's arrow, the leading line the move follows drawn through the objects that lead it, suns at the emitter positions), PANEL 4 a SCALE STRIP (the lead actor at panel-1 and panel-2 size on one baseline beside a head-unit ruler, plus the radiance and accent swatches of the D74 pair). `out` is `out/<shot>-layout-<NN>.png`. Measure on the sheet: the lead actor's height in panels 1 and 2 as percent of panel height and in heads (against model.json), the emitter position in each panel as a fraction of panel width and height, the panel-3 camera arrow direction against the shot's move type; reject and regenerate once if the figure's panel-1 height is off the camera row's size by more than 10 points or the hue is not the D74 pair. Write `v3/layouts/<shot>.json` (camera start and end in words, move and led_by, hue, emitter start and end positions, figure heights, heads, panels, cards, sheet sha256, receipt, provisional: true), copy the sheet to `assets/layouts/<shot>-layout-<NN>.png` and `public/assets/layouts/`, lay it into the `LayoutSheet` composition and render one still. The key sheet of this shot is drawn at this camera; the render study measures against this file (C25). The owner approves the sheet from the still.
 
 Return: Camera (start, end, move, led by); Emitter; Figure Heights (panel 1, panel 2, heads); Hue; Cards Used (eagle ids); Sheet Path; layout.json Path; Generation Receipt; Rejected Generations; Concerns.
\ No newline at end of file

```
